description.narrative: 1. Regional DP: Establishes a Sub-regional Network of Safe Schools in Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador and Peru, aligned with the Comprehensive Global Framework for School Safety. Focuses on intergovernmental dialogue, monitoring the Safe School Declaration in conflict zones, and providing training to address risks. Actions include regional forums, knowledge-sharing, and a communication campaign to enhance awareness and risk management. 2. National DP: Aims to improve disaster preparedness and response within education systems. Collaborates with Disaster Risk Management Committees in high-risk schools to update safety plans and trains teachers and stakeholders in crisis management and resilience. Emphasizes children’s empowerment and infrastructural improvements to create safe, resilient, inclusive learning environments. 3. EiE: Enhances access and retention in safe learning settings, especially in vulnerable, violence-affected, and disaster-prone communities. Supports back-to-school campaigns, identifies at-risk children, and provides tailored interventions to prevent dropouts. Integrates protection measures and feedback mechanisms for accountability, and includes a crisis modifier to adapt aid, ensuring education continuity in crises.

Result 1: Promotion and Implementation of the Safe Schools Model (SSM) - Sector: Disaster Risk reduction (DRR) / Disaster Preparedness (DP) • R.1.A.1: Launch a sub-regional Safe Schools initiative using the Comprehensive Global Framework for School Safety, including a roadmap developed at a high-level forum. • R.1.A.2: Systematize and share best practices and lessons from school safety and disaster preparedness via the Regional Education Group. • R.1.A.3: Generate evidence on the impact of violence in educational settings within multi-hazard contexts and adapt policies for violence and disaster risk management in schools. • R.1.A.4: Host a Second High-Level Forum to promote and monitor Safe Schools Initiative implementation. • R.1.A.5: Develop a communication strategy with community-led awareness campaigns and promotional materials. • R.1.A.6: Provide technical support to national institutions and disaster risk management systems in participating countries. Result 2: Enhanced Preparedness in Education Systems - Sector: DRR/DP • R.2.A.1: Improve disaster risk management plans in high-risk schools, incorporating gender perspectives. • R.2.A.2: Train teachers and stakeholders on disaster and violence response within school environments. • R.2.A.3: Educate students on disaster preparedness through play-based learning and life skills activities. • R.2.A.4: Upgrade school infrastructure based on Safe School Facilities assessments. Result 3: Improved Access and Retention for At-Risk Children - Sector: Education in Emergencies • R.3.A.1: Implement back-to-school campaigns and ensure safe, inclusive education access. • R.3.A.2: Identify and support out-of-school children in disaster and violence-prone areas, coordinating with local authorities. • R.3.A.3: Train education staff on child-centered methods, psychosocial support, and gender-sensitive practices. • R.3.A.4: Provide conditional cash assistance and vouchers to support enrollment and attendance in Colombia and Peru. • R.3.A.5: Offer remedial education programs for at-risk children. • R.3.A.6: Establish gender-sensitive and child-friendly feedback mechanisms in schools. • R.3.A.7: Develop multi-sectoral referral pathways and train staff on protecting children with special needs. Result 4: Strengthened Socio-Emotional Learning (ASE) - Sector: Education in Emergencies • R.4.A.1: Enhance teacher capacities to support students’ psycho-emotional needs in selected schools. • R.4.A.2: Build children’s self-protection and violence response skills. • R.4.A.3: Train DECE members in conflict-sensitive psycho-social support. • R.4.A.4: Improve school infrastructure in Quito and Guayaquil to address natural and man-made threats. Result 5: Strengthened Inter-Institutional Coordination - Sector: Protection • R.5.A.1: Develop protocols to improve institutional coordination with the educational community against natural and man-made threats. • R.5.A.2: Implement a communication plan with key messages on violence prevention and self-protection. • R.5.A.3: Coordinate with local Emergency Operations Committees and violence response groups. • R.5.A.4: Conduct high-level meetings to share and evaluate safe educational community practices. • R.5.A.5: Work with local governments to enhance school and community infrastructure. Result 6: Promoting Community Co-Responsibility for Child Protection - Sector: DRR/DP • R.6.A.1: Conduct risk assessments, create intervention reports, and develop action plans with community participation. • R.6.A.2: Lead community activities to boost awareness and responsibility for disaster risk reduction and resilience. • R.6.A.3: Facilitate practical exercises to enhance response capacities and change behavioral habits within the educational community. Result 7: Contingency Planning and Immediate Lifesaving Support (Crisis Modifier) • R.7.A.1: Implement alert and assessment procedures for emergencies. • R.7.A.2: Procure and deploy emergency response resources swiftly.

SUMMARY This regional project, implemented in Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador and Peru, aims to contribute to improving safe and inclusive access to education for all children and adolescents in disaster prone regions as well as educational continuity during and after emergencies. The project will initiate the establishment of a sub-regional network of Safe Schools in the Andean Subregion, aligning with the 2022-2030 Comprehensive School Safety initiative and contributing to the Worldwide Initiative on Safe Schools (WISS). The region faces multiple and overlapping crises, threatening access to education and retention, creating an urgent need for more resilient communities enabled to face natural and human-made disasters while addressing protection concerns. The project will offer a comprehensive, multi-hazard and multi-threat people-centred response that integrates disaster risk reduction, education in emergencies and protection.

The Andes region is the world's second-most disaster-prone area, with natural hazards worsened by poverty, inequality, violence, conflict, civil unrest, weak economies, and limited government response. 1. Bolivia: Natural hazards like droughts, fires, and floods hinder education access, increase migration, and damage infrastructure. Out-of-school children, especially girls, children with disabilities, and migrants, face risks due to poverty, violence, and inadequate facilities. 2. Colombia: Armed conflict and violence in regions like Chocó and Cauca disrupt education. Risks include child recruitment by armed groups, SGBV, landmines, and poor infrastructure, affecting access and retention, especially for girls and children with disabilities. 3. Peru: Migrant children in areas like Piura and Tumbes face economic hardship, lack of documentation, and inadequate support. Issues such as child labor, early marriage, violence, and poor infrastructure threaten education, particularly during floods. 4. Ecuador: Rising violence has increased child fatalities and dropout rates. Schools lack safety measures and trained staff to support vulnerable students, with operational challenges due to limited resources and local training.

The DRR approach of the project seeks to build resilience within education systems and communities, not only for immediate response to disasters but also as part of a larger strategy to minimize the long-term impact of emergencies, reduce vulnerabilities, and integrate DRR efforts into broader development initiatives. Education in emergency interventions aim to restore and expand access to safe and inclusive learning environments. Providing a protective environment, schools offer normality, structure, and psychosocial support, playing a crucial role in identifying and responding to protection concerns like child recruitment, GBV, and exploitation. By investing in education, especially for girls, the intervention empowers, builds resilience and fosters community cohesion for stability and development. Finally, by integrating a protection approach, the project will respond, prevent and respond to various forms of SEA. A specific focus is put on engaging educational structures and communities in identification, referrals and raising awareness around children’s concerns in emergency contexts, thus promoting awareness and mobilizing support to prevent and address child protection concerns in the longer term.

The project's beneficiaries include Ministries of Education, DRM entities, the Secretariat of the Andean Community, Regional Education Group, youth representatives, donors, and CSOs. In Bolivia, Colombia, Peru, it targets communities facing complex emergencies, natural disasters, violence, displacement, focusing on out-of-school children, school staff, local authorities.

The proposed project complements ongoing initiatives by enhancing existing efforts and integrating lessons learned across regions. In Bolivia, the project builds on a DG ECHO-funded initiative to enhance emergency preparedness in Guaraní municipalities, sharing resources with UNDP and focusing on areas affected by multiple risks. It leverages participatory methods to develop school contingency plans and microprojects. In Peru, it aligns with ongoing projects in Piura and Tumbes funded by UNICEF, UNHCR, and others, focusing on child protection and community-based mechanisms. The project will link with existing interventions to improve efficiency and impact, drawing from past flood response experience and local partnerships. In Colombia, the project aligns with Plan’s existing humanitarian and development portfolio, including five ongoing development projects. It will also complement the ECW’s MYRP if approved, ensuring no overlaps. In Ecuador, the project builds on collaboration with MINEDUC, drawing from previous ECHO-funded projects that developed disaster preparedness tools and a management model for Safe Schools, while leveraging the PI Early Action Fund and other preparedness projects.
